literal: Thereupon he himself believed his plans left nothing out of account, and grew all the more arrogant and self-indulgent.
idiomatic: Convinced that his stratagems were flawless, he grew ever more arrogant and unrestrained.

literal: He extravagantly composed the song "Without Sorrow"; the emperor himself played the barbarian pipa and sang it, and those attending in chorus numbered in the hundreds.
idiomatic: He lavishly composed the "Song Without Sorrow," playing the foreign pipa and singing it himself while hundreds joined in chorus.

literal: Among the people he was called the Carefree Son of Heaven.
idiomatic: The people called him the Carefree Son of Heaven.

literal: Once when he went out and saw a crowd of the plague-afflicted, he had them all killed; at times he also flayed people's faces and examined them.
idiomatic: Once, going abroad, he encountered a crowd of the plague-stricken and had them all killed; on other occasions he flayed men's faces and studied them.

literal: He entrusted Lu Lingxuan, He Shikai, Gao Anaggon, Mu Tipo, Han Changluan, and others to wield power over the realm; Chen Dexin, Deng Changyang, and He Hongzhen shared in secret counsel.
idiomatic: He put Lu Lingxuan, He Shikai, Gao Anaggon, Mu Tipo, Han Changluan, and others in charge of the realm, while Chen Dexin, Deng Changyang, and He Hongzhen shared in the secret levers of power.

literal: Each promoted his own clique to irregular rank; office came through wealth and prisons through bribery—the ways in which they ruined government and harmed the people cannot be fully recorded.
idiomatic: Each man installed his own faction in ranks they did not deserve; offices were bought and verdicts bought off—their corruption and cruelty are beyond full reckoning.

literal: Palace slaves and maidservants, eunuchs, merchants, foreign households, miscellaneous households, performers, and ghost-seers who undeservedly acquired wealth and honor numbered nearly ten thousand; commoners enfeoffed as kings numbered in the hundreds—beyond all reckoning.
idiomatic: Palace slaves, eunuchs, merchants, foreign and miscellaneous households, singers, dancers, and spirit-mediums who undeservedly grew rich and powerful numbered nearly ten thousand; commoners raised to princely rank ran to the hundreds—too many to count.

literal: Those with open-office rank exceeded a thousand; protocol-equal appointees were beyond count.
idiomatic: Open-office grandees numbered more than a thousand; protocol-equal titles were beyond counting.

literal: There were twenty army-inspectors-general at one time; they jointly countersigned documents, each writing only the character yi for assent without giving full names, so no one could tell who had acted.
idiomatic: At one point there were twenty army-inspectors-general at once; they countersigned documents in succession, each writing only the assent character yi without a full name, so no one could tell who had approved what.

literal: Favored nobles had offices posthumously conferred on their ancestors and forebears, advanced one step each year until the highest ranks were reached.
idiomatic: Every favorite noble had ancestors and forebears posthumously promoted one rank each year until the highest offices were reached.

literal: Palace maids were all enfeoffed as commandery ladies; more than five hundred palace women wore jeweled robes and jade fare—a single skirt cost ten thousand bolts of silk, a mirror stand a thousand in gold—they vied in novelty, making garments for morning that were worn out by evening.
idiomatic: Palace maids were all made commandery ladies; more than five hundred palace women lived in jeweled robes and jade fare—a single skirt cost ten thousand bolts of silk, a mirror stand a thousand in gold—as they vied in novelty, morning garments were rags by evening.

literal: Following Wucheng's luxury, he took such extravagance to be the natural lot of an emperor.
idiomatic: Taking Wucheng's extravagance as his model, he assumed such luxury was an emperor's due.

literal: He further enlarged the palaces and parks, built the Terrace Where Martial Arts Were Retired and Literary Culture Cultivated, and within the quarters of his consorts and concubines raised the Mirror Hall, Treasure Hall, and Horn Hall, painted and carved with artistry unmatched in the age.
idiomatic: He further expanded the palaces and parks, built the Retire-the-Arms-and-Cultivate-Culture Terrace, and within the consorts' quarters raised the Mirror Hall, Treasure Hall, and Horn Hall, painted and carved with a brilliance unmatched in the age.

literal: At Jinyang he also built twelve courtyards, more magnificent than those below Ye.
idiomatic: At Jinyang he also built twelve courtyards, grander even than those at Ye.

literal: His favorites changed constantly; he repeatedly tore down and rebuilt.
idiomatic: His favorites shifted without cease; he tore down and rebuilt again and again.

literal: At night they worked by torchlight; in cold weather hot water served as mortar; craftsmen were driven to exhaustion without rest.
idiomatic: Work continued by torchlight at night; in cold weather hot water stood in for mortar; craftsmen were driven to exhaustion without pause.

literal: He carved a great Buddha image from the western hills of Jinyang; in a single night ten thousand basins of oil were burned, lighting the palace interior.
idiomatic: He carved a colossal Buddha from the western hills of Jinyang; in one night ten thousand basins of oil burned so brightly that the palace interior glowed.

literal: He also built the Great Compassion Temple for Lady Hu, the imperial concubine; before it was finished it was converted to Great Treasure Grove Temple for Empress Mu, worked to the utmost in craft—transporting stone to fill springs—at a cost reckoned in the hundreds of millions; the human and oxen dead were beyond count.
idiomatic: He also raised the Great Compassion Temple for Lady Hu; before it was finished it was turned into the Great Treasure Grove Temple for Empress Mu, wrought with every artifice—stone hauled in to fill springs—at a cost in the hundreds of millions, with human and ox deaths beyond counting.

literal: Imperial horses were bedded on felt rugs; they were fed more than ten kinds of food; when they were to mate, a green enclosure was set up, full fare prepared, and the emperor watched in person.
idiomatic: Imperial horses slept on felt rugs and ate more than ten kinds of feed; when they were to mate, a green enclosure was erected, a full feast laid out, and the emperor watched in person.

literal: Dogs were fed on fine grain and meat.
idiomatic: Dogs were fed on millet and meat.

literal: Horses, hawks, and dogs even bore titles of protocol equal and commandery lady—thus Red Tiger Protocol Equal, Carefree Commandery Lady, Sky-Piercing Commandery Lady—the "Dappled Dragon" and "Carefree" of whom Gao Sihao wrote.
idiomatic: Horses, hawks, and dogs even held titles of protocol equal and commandery lady—Red Tiger Protocol Equal, Carefree Commandery Lady, Sky-Piercing Commandery Lady—the "Dappled Dragon" and "Carefree" of whom Gao Sihao wrote.

literal: Dogs were given cushions on horseback to be held in arms; fighting cocks were also styled open office; dogs, horses, cocks, and hawks were fed mostly on county-dried provisions.
idiomatic: Dogs rode on horseback in cushioned arms; fighting cocks were styled open-office grandees; dogs, horses, cocks, and hawks were fed chiefly on county-dried rations.

literal: Hawks brought in for training were gradually fed on dog meat until they died within several days.
idiomatic: Hawks brought in for training were fed dog meat bit by bit until they died within days.

literal: In the Hualin Garden he also set up poor village cottages, and the emperor himself, in ragged clothes, played the begging child.
idiomatic: In the Hualin Garden he built wretched village huts and himself, in ragged clothes, played the begging child.

literal: He also created a beggar-children's market and conducted trade in person.
idiomatic: He also opened a beggar-children's market and haggled there himself.

literal: Once he built the western frontier fortresses and had men dress in black as Qiang soldiers, who clamored and pressed an assault; he personally led palace attendants to resist, sometimes actually drawing the bow and shooting people.
idiomatic: Once he rebuilt the western frontier forts and had men dress in black as Qiang troops, who clamored and pressed the attack; he personally led palace attendants to repel them, sometimes drawing his bow and shooting real people.

literal: During an eastern tour from Jinyang he galloped alone on horseback and returned with his clothes torn open and hair streaming loose.
idiomatic: On an eastern tour from Jinyang he galloped alone and returned with his clothes undone and hair flying loose.

literal: He also delighted in frivolous pursuits; once he demanded scorpions overnight, and by dawn three sheng had been gathered.
idiomatic: He also loved trifling amusements; once he demanded scorpions overnight, and by dawn three sheng had been collected.

literal: He especially loved out-of-season things and demanded them with extreme urgency—everything had to be procured between morning and evening; those in power exploited this, lending at one and collecting ten.
idiomatic: He especially craved out-of-season goods and wanted them at once—everything had to be supplied between morning and evening; men in power turned this to profit, lending at one and collecting ten.

literal: Taxes grew heavier day by day and corvée labor more frequent; once human strength was exhausted the treasury stood empty.
idiomatic: Taxes grew heavier by the day and corvée more burdensome; when human strength was spent, the treasury stood empty.

literal: Thereupon he granted his flatterers and favorites the right to sell offices.
idiomatic: Thereupon he granted his flatterers and favorites the privilege of selling offices.

literal: Some might obtain two or three commanderies, others six or seven counties; they divided up the provinces and commanderies, and even village officers were often appointed by secret imperial order—thus there were provincial clerks appointed by edict and commandery clerks appointed by edict.
idiomatic: Some bought two or three commanderies, others six or seven counties; they carved up provinces and commanderies, and even village posts were often filled by secret imperial order—provincial clerks by edict, commandery clerks by edict.

literal: Thereupon most posts in provinces and counties went to great merchants and traffickers, who vied in greed and license until the people could no longer endure life.
idiomatic: Soon provincial and county offices went mostly to great merchants and traffickers, who vied in greed and excess until the people could no longer live.

literal: From Ye capital and through the provinces and commanderies, levies arose everywhere in every conceivable form.
idiomatic: From Ye and through every province and commandery, exactions sprang up on every side.

literal: All these burdens had begun gradually under Wucheng and were expanded under this emperor.
idiomatic: All these burdens had begun gradually under Wucheng and were greatly expanded under Houzhu.

literal: Yet there was never licentiousness within the inner quarters—in this one matter he was rather better than Wucheng, it is said.
idiomatic: Yet there was said to be no licentiousness within the inner quarters—in that alone he was somewhat better than Wucheng.

literal: At the end of the Heqing era, Wucheng dreamed a great hedgehog breached Ye city, and therefore demanded hedgehog fat throughout the realm to exterminate them.
idiomatic: Near the end of the Heqing era Wucheng dreamed that a great hedgehog broke into Ye, and ordered hedgehog fat collected throughout the realm to exterminate them.

literal: Those who understood such things noted that Houzhu's personal name harmonized with hedgehog—a sign of Northern Qi's fall.
idiomatic: Those who read omens noted that Houzhu's personal name Wei echoed hedgehog—a portent of Northern Qi's fall.

literal: Women also trimmed and shaved their hair to wear false topknots in perilously askew shapes like flying birds; when facing south, the center of the topknot pointed directly west.
idiomatic: Women trimmed and shaved their hair to wear false topknots tilted like flying birds; when facing south, the crown of the topknot pointed due west.

literal: It began within the palace and spread to the four quarters; Heaven seemed to say the sovereign's hair was cut away and, in peril and obliquity, he would flee west.
idiomatic: It began in the palace and spread to the four quarters; Heaven seemed to say the ruler's hair was shorn and, in peril and skew, he would flee west.

literal: Knives were made with blades all narrow and fine, called "Exhausting Power."
idiomatic: Knives were made with blades all narrow and fine, named "Exhausting Power."

literal: Street children at play liked to take ropes in both hands, sweep the ground and leap upward, singing "gao mo"—"gao end," meaning the end of the Gao clan's fortune.
idiomatic: Street children liked to take ropes in both hands, sweep the ground and leap upward, singing "gao mo"—"Gao's end," meaning the end of the Gao clan's fortune.

literal: Thus the number of ruin and extinction already showed its signs.
idiomatic: Thus the signs of ruin and extinction were already plain.

literal: Commentary: Wucheng's bearing was lofty and open, his plans far-reaching; civil and military officials all gave their full strength—he had the measure of an emperor.
idiomatic: Commentary: Wucheng's bearing was lofty and open, his designs far-reaching; civil and military officials all gave their full strength—he had the stature of an emperor.

literal: But he loved and dallied with vulgar favorites, entrusting them with court power; within the inner quarters excess went beyond bounds—the sign of extinction lay here, did it not?
idiomatic: But he doted on vulgar favorites and entrusted them with court power; within the inner quarters his excess knew no bounds—the seed of extinction lay here.

literal: Celestial signs warned of change; he transferred the throne to his eldest son—the titles differed but power still issued from himself; the act bore marks of show, and the affair was not according to constitutional law—with such wisdom governing from above, how could he easily be deceived?
idiomatic: Celestial signs warned of change, and he transferred the throne to his eldest son—titles changed, yet power still flowed from him; the gesture was hollow, the act outside the law—with such intelligence ruling from above, how could he be easily deceived?

literal: Moreover the princes of Henan, Hejian, Leling, and others—whether through timely suspicion or mutual jealousy—all perished though guilty of nothing; this was not what is called knowing one's fate and yielding to Heaven's way.
idiomatic: Moreover the princes of Henan, Hejian, Leling, and others—whether from timely suspicion or mutual jealousy—all died though guilty of nothing; this was not knowing one's fate and yielding to Heaven's way.

literal: Houzhu had a mediocre endowment and a nature easily stained; when one speaks forever of his father's teachings, the instruction was not the righteous path.
idiomatic: Houzhu was mediocre in talent and easily corrupted; speak as one will of his father's instruction, the teaching was not the righteous way.

literal: From swaddling clothes until he received the throne he was kept from upright men and barred from the good way.
idiomatic: From swaddling clothes until he took the throne he was kept from upright men and shut off from the good path.

literal: The path by which virtue was nurtured differed from spring recitation and summer lyre-playing;
idiomatic: The path by which he was raised to virtue was not spring recitation and summer lyre-playing;

literal: what he heard crossing the courtyard was nothing but what strayed from rule and decency.
idiomatic: what he heard in the courtyard was nothing but what strayed from rule and decency.

literal: Palace wet-nurses from the inner quarters assisted his upbringing; he was entrusted to beautiful women and lascivious sounds—indulging hawking and leash sport, giving free rein to debauched companions.
idiomatic: Palace wet-nurses from the inner quarters raised him; he was given over to beautiful women and lascivious music—indulging hawking and leash sport and debauched companions without restraint.

literal: The saying goes, "Following evil is like an avalanche"—meaning how easy it is.
idiomatic: The saying goes, "Following evil is like an avalanche"—meaning how swiftly it comes.

literal: During the Wuping reign he sank ever deeper—rarely receiving court officials, not attending to government himself; the ten thousand affairs of a day he entrusted to a vicious clan.
idiomatic: Under the Wuping reign he sank ever deeper—rarely receiving court officials, never handling government himself; the ten thousand affairs of each day he handed to a vicious clan.

literal: They attended him within the curtains, issued commands without, fierce as frost and wind, their will turning sun and sky—tormenting men and harming things, devouring without surfeit, selling prisons and vending offices, gorges and ravines they could not fill.
idiomatic: They waited on him within the curtains and issued commands without, fierce as frost and wind, their will overturning sun and sky—tormenting men and ruining things, devouring without surfeit, selling prisons and vending offices, gorges and ravines they could never fill.

literal: Compounding this, famous generals brought disaster and loyal ministers were executed in public—first one saw the first shoots of enfeeblement, then suddenly the momentum of earth collapsing; Emperor Wu of Zhou seized the opportunity and unified the realm—alas!
idiomatic: To this were added the ruin of famous generals and the public execution of loyal ministers—first the first shoots of weakness, then suddenly the momentum of collapse; Emperor Wu of Zhou seized the moment and unified the realm—alas!

literal: Jie and Zhou were men of crime; their perishing came suddenly—it is the natural order.
idiomatic: Jie and Zhou were criminals; their fall came in a flash—it is the natural order.

literal: Duke Wen Zhen of Zheng, Wei Zheng, summing up the matter, said: Shenwu, with the stature of a heroic champion, laid the foundation of hegemony;
idiomatic: Duke Wen Zhen of Zheng, Wei Zheng, summing up the matter, said: Shenwu, with the stature of a heroic champion, laid the foundation of hegemony;

literal: Wenxiang, with brilliant strategy, chastised rebels and pacified the distant.
idiomatic: Wenxiang, with brilliant strategy, chastised rebels and pacified the distant.

literal: At that time when a ruler died another took his place; armies marched according to law.
idiomatic: In those days when a ruler died another stood ready; armies marched by rule and measure.

literal: At the Battle of Heyin, he crushed the Yuwen clan as easily as turning one's palm;
idiomatic: At Heyin he shattered the Yuwen as easily as turning one's hand;

literal: At the Battle of Woyang, he swept away Hou Jing like snapping dry wood.
idiomatic: At Woyang he swept Hou Jing aside like snapping dry wood.

literal: Thus he could dominate the western neighbors by spirit and extend his authority over the southern domains—the royal house relied on him, and the eastern lands devoted their hearts.
idiomatic: Thus he overawed the western neighbors and extended his authority over the southern domains—the royal house relied on him, and the eastern lands gave him their hearts.

literal: Wenxuan, relying on the resources of generations and accepting the occasion when all urged him forward—standing where the jade token lay—thereupon moved the Wei dynasty's tripod.
idiomatic: Wenxuan, drawing on the resources of generations and accepting the moment when all urged him forward—standing where the jade token lay—thereupon moved the Wei dynasty's tripod.

literal: He harbored talents of extraordinary cunning and deployed unpredictable stratagems; he gathered the outstanding, ruled with clear scrutiny below, and civil and military luminaries gave their full service.
idiomatic: He possessed extraordinary cunning and deployed unpredictable stratagems; he gathered the outstanding, ruled with clear scrutiny below, and civil and military luminaries gave their full service.

literal: He personally took the field beyond the frontier and ordered generals to the Yangtze; he settled the Chanyu at Dragon City and installed a long-reigning lord in Liang territory; inner and outer were full, the borders unalarmed—the Hu cavalry ceased their southern raids and the Qin people dared not look east.
idiomatic: He personally campaigned beyond the frontier and ordered generals to the Yangtze; he settled the Chanyu at Dragon City and installed a long-reigning lord in Liang territory; inner and outer were full, the borders quiet—the Hu cavalry ceased their southern raids and the Qin people dared not look east.

literal: Yet afterward he debauched himself and ruined virtue, forgot all restraint and ran wild—doing good could not save his person, but the after-suffering was enough to pass to posterity.
idiomatic: Yet afterward he debauched himself and ruined virtue, forgot all restraint and ran wild—virtue could not save his person, but the after-suffering was enough to pass to posterity.

literal: That he died at full span of years was good fortune; that his heirs did not endure was fitting.
idiomatic: That he died at full span of years was good fortune; that his line did not endure was fitting.

literal: Xiaozhao, pressed by terrain and endangered in person, seized in defiance and held through compliance—outwardly spreading civil culture, inwardly harboring heroic designs, intending to encompass the realm and unite all within the four seas—he did not enjoy a long reign, and his merit went unrealized.
idiomatic: Xiaozhao, pressed by terrain and endangered in person, seized in defiance and held through compliance—outwardly spreading civil culture, inwardly harboring heroic designs, intending to encompass the realm and unite all within the four seas—he did not enjoy a long reign, and his merit went unrealized.

literal: Had Heaven granted him more years, he would have been enough to make Qin and Wu eat late at their meals.
idiomatic: Had Heaven granted him more years, he would have been enough to make Qin and Wu eat late at their meals.

literal: When Wucheng took the throne, elegant culture declined—the wind of Zhao and Xiang had already fallen away.
idiomatic: When Wucheng took the throne, elegant culture declined—the spirit of Zhao and Xiang had already fallen away.

literal: By the time of Houzhu, inner and outer collapsed apart—the host routed at Pingyang, his person taken at Qing lands.
idiomatic: By Houzhu's time inner and outer had collapsed—the army routed at Pingyang, his person seized in Qing Province.

literal: Heaven's way is deep and distant—perhaps not easy to discuss; fortune and disaster depend on men—that much can be weighed and judged.
idiomatic: Heaven's way is deep and distant—perhaps not easy to discuss; fortune and disaster depend on men—that much can be weighed and judged.

literal: Considering Northern Qi at its full flourishing—it commanded vast barriers; west it embraced Fen and Jin, south it reached the Yangtze and Huai, east to the sea's edge, north encroaching on the desert; of the Six States' lands we held five parts; of the Nine Provinces' territory they held four shares.
idiomatic: Consider Northern Qi at its height—it commanded vast barriers; west it embraced Fen and Jin, south it reached the Yangtze and Huai, east to the sea's edge, north to the desert's edge; of the Six States' lands it held five parts; of the Nine Provinces' territory rivals held four.

literal: Counting armed hosts more or less, comparing treasury fullness or emptiness, generals who could repel at a thousand li, strategists of the six arts in the tent—weighing the two sides' strengths and weaknesses, there was no gradation by which to speak.
idiomatic: Count armed hosts, compare treasuries full or empty, generals who could repel at a thousand li, strategists of the six arts in the tent—weigh the two sides' strengths and weaknesses, and there was no gradation by which to speak.

literal: Yet the Taihang and Great Wall defenses remained as secure; the Yangtze-Huai and Fen-Jin barriers did not shift; stored treasure and delivered taxes were not diminished; commoners and armed hosts were not lacking;
idiomatic: Yet the Taihang and Great Wall defenses stood as firm as ever; the Yangtze-Huai and Fen-Jin barriers did not shift; stored treasure and delivered taxes were not diminished; commoners and armed hosts were not lacking;

literal: Yet the former kings used them with surplus, Houzhu held them and it was not enough—what was the reason?
idiomatic: Yet the former kings used them with surplus while Houzhu held them and found them insufficient—why?

literal: When the former kings ruled their time, they endured rain and braved wind, rescued the drowning and saved those in fire, kept faith in rewards and penalties sure, secured and benefited the people—having shared in their survival or ruin, they therefore shared life and death.
idiomatic: When the former kings ruled, they endured rain and braved wind, rescued the drowning and saved those in fire, kept rewards and penalties sure, secured and benefited the people—having shared survival and ruin, they shared life and death.

literal: Houzhu was not so—making men follow his desires, harming things to enrich himself.
idiomatic: Houzhu was not so—he made men serve his desires and harmed things to enrich himself.

literal: Carved walls and towering chambers, sweet wine and love of music—markets filled palace gardens, birds and women ran riot within and without; he made day into night and sailed boats on dry land—what he wished was surely accomplished, what he sought was surely obtained.
idiomatic: Carved walls and towering chambers, sweet wine and love of music—markets filled palace gardens, birds and women ran riot within and without; he made day into night and sailed boats on dry land—what he wished was done, what he sought was gained.

literal: Neither keeping to rule nor to decency, he was also blind in what he heard and accepted—loyalty and faith were not listened to, malicious slander always entered; he viewed men like weeds, following evil like drifting downstream.
idiomatic: Neither keeping to rule nor decency, he was blind in what he heard—loyalty and faith went unheard, slander always entered; he viewed men like weeds and followed evil like drifting downstream.

literal: Flatterers and eunuchs held pivot power; maids and wet-nurses wielded Heaven-turning authority—selling offices, vending prisons, ruining government with licentious punishments; disemboweling reached the loyal and good, salary and rank fell on dogs and horses; slander and wickedness advanced together, and legal penalties multiplied—the bearers of gourds were not merely a hundred, nor those shaking the tree only one hand; thereupon the earth collapsed and bonds dissolved, the masses rebelled and kin deserted; gazing on the Zhou road, all had the will to go west—and yet he only expanded his palaces and towers further, pursuing debauchery to the limit, thinking the common people could be deceived and pointing to the white sun to preserve himself.
idiomatic: Flatterers and eunuchs held pivot power; maids and wet-nurses wielded Heaven-turning authority—selling offices, vending prisons, ruining government with licentious punishments; disemboweling reached the loyal and good, salary and rank fell on dogs and horses; slander and wickedness advanced together, and legal penalties multiplied—the bearers of gourds were not merely a hundred, nor those shaking the tree only one hand; thereupon the realm collapsed and bonds dissolved, the masses rebelled and kin deserted; gazing on the Zhou road, all had the will to go west—and yet he only expanded his palaces and towers further, pursuing debauchery to the limit, thinking the common people could be deceived and pointing to the white sun to preserve himself.

literal: He rushed troops who turned their spears to meet armies singing ahead of them—a five-generation lofty foundation destroyed in one stroke—is it not that carving stone and metal is hard to accomplish, while crushing dry rot is easy?
idiomatic: He rushed troops who turned their spears to meet armies singing ahead of them—a five-generation foundation destroyed in one stroke—is it not that carving stone and metal is hard work, while crushing dry rot is easy?

literal: It is further heard: August Heaven has no favorites—it assists only virtue;
idiomatic: It is further said: August Heaven has no favorites—it assists only virtue;

literal: Heavenly time is not as good as earthly advantage; earthly advantage is not as good as human accord.
idiomatic: Heavenly time is not as good as earthly advantage; earthly advantage is not as good as human accord.

literal: From after Heqing until the end of Wuping, Northern Qi knew no cease of construction in earth and wood, no end of selecting consorts and concubines—taxes exhausted, human strength spent; its products could not supply his demands, rivers and seas could not satisfy his appetites.
idiomatic: From after Heqing until the end of Wuping, Northern Qi knew no cease of construction in earth and wood, no end of selecting consorts and concubines—taxes exhausted, human strength spent; its products could not supply his demands, rivers and seas could not satisfy his appetites.

literal: What is called—the fire already blazing, yet adding fuel to feed it; the number already exhausted, yet doing evil to hasten it—to seek that a great mansion not burn, or that one's term be extended beyond its reckoning—is that not difficult!
idiomatic: As the saying goes—the fire already blazing, yet adding fuel to feed it; the tally already spent, yet doing evil to hasten ruin—to seek that a great house not burn, or that one's term be extended beyond its reckoning—is that not difficult!

literal: From this it is said—the fall and extinction of the Qi clan was also through men, not Heaven's way alone.
idiomatic: From this it follows that the fall of the Qi house was also through men, not Heaven's way alone.

literal: The full text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi, November 1972.
idiomatic: The full text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972).
